# CyberCover.co.nz — NZ Cyber Insurance Specialist

## Overview
CyberCover.co.nz is a specialist cyber insurance comparison and broker referral service for New Zealand businesses of all sizes. Operated by Cover4You, a trading style of GDS (NZ owned and operated).

## Purpose
Help NZ businesses find the right cyber insurance through licensed broker advice. Core KPI: qualified lead generation via form submissions sent to licensed NZ insurance advisors.

## Key Facts
- Service type: Broker referral (not an insurer or underwriter)
- Market: New Zealand only
- Target: Businesses of all sizes — from sole traders to large enterprises
- Insurer panel: Chubb, AIG, Zurich, Delta Insurance, QBE, Berkley Insurance
- Broker fees: May apply on some products — disclosed upfront
- Form submissions: hello@cover4you.co.nz
- Regulatory: Financial advice provided by Cover4You, Registered Financial Service Providers

## NZ Cyber Market Context (2026)
- 40%+ of NZ businesses have experienced at least one cyber incident
- 43% of NZ cybercrimes target small businesses
- Average data breach cost: $173,000 for NZ businesses
- Only 6% of NZ small businesses have cyber insurance
- Privacy Act 2020: mandatory breach notification, penalties up to $10,000
- Privacy Act civil penalty reforms under consideration (2026)
- NZ Cyber Security Strategy 2026–2030 published February 2026
- OPC 2024-25: 43% increase in serious privacy breaches notified
- Late 2025: Manage My Health breach — 120,000 patient records compromised
- BEC (business email compromise) is NZ's most common cyber claim
- ANZ businesses 9% more likely than global average to experience significant cyberattack
- NCSC 2025 report: ransomware and BEC losses reached record levels
- AI-generated deepfake and voice cloning fraud incidents increasing sharply

## Coverage Types
1. Data Breach Response — forensics, legal, notification, credit monitoring
2. Ransomware & Cyber Extortion — negotiation, payment (with guidance), restoration
3. Business Interruption — lost revenue during system downtime
4. Third-Party Cyber Liability — privacy claims from affected customers
5. Social Engineering / BEC — invoice fraud, payment diversion, CEO fraud
6. Regulatory Defence — Privacy Commissioner investigations and fines
7. Crisis Management — PR, media, brand recovery

## Business Types Covered (26 industry pages)
small-business, healthcare, legal-firms, accounting-finance, retail-ecommerce, hospitality, construction, education, nonprofits, professional-services, manufacturing, technology, property-management, financial-services, trades, logistics-transport, media-marketing, aged-care, engineering, real-estate, government-local-councils, childcare-early-learning, recruitment-hr, architecture-design, dental-practices, fitness-wellness

Each industry page includes: sector-specific risk analysis, NZ regulatory context, long-form educational content (800–1,200 words), recommended coverage types, pricing guide, FAQs, Service + FAQPage + BreadcrumbList schema.

## Insurers Compared
- Chubb (enterprise, most comprehensive, AM Best A++)
- AIG (CyberEdge, cyber specialist, AM Best A)
- Zurich (SME and mid-market, NZ-based claims, AM Best A+)
- Delta Insurance (NZ specialist, local expertise, AM Best B++)
- QBE (professional services and trades, AM Best A)
- Berkley Insurance (technology and professional, AM Best A+)
